players.message: Congrats on the round. Your spinner hit hard and fast, so I will rethink the design: a sturdier, lower robot with more armor on top and a better way to get under you. I expect a close, clean rematch.
players.reasoning:
I'm picturing the Cyclone as a 107 kg vertical spinner with a 0.4 radius disc and 8000 W behind it, which is what flipped us over in the last round. The main danger is that disc hitting our front, so I'm weighing front and top armor plus maybe a wedge, though it's unclear whether a 50 kJ structure can really hold against that.

I'm working out the opponent's rim speed: about 84 m/s at 2000 rpm with a 0.4 radius, which means a lot of energy. I'm weighing a sturdy, low, wide robot with armor on every face and an invertible design, since being flipped onto a side is what knocked us out and a side-lying robot can't drive or self-right.

I'm working through the spinner's damage, and I'm weighing steel plating at the front since it absorbs a lot per hit. I'm sketching a 0.9 by 0.6 by 0.3 m layout and tallying the mass for frame, drive, battery and armor against the 110 kg limit.

I'm checking the mass of the armor options: steel on top would be too heavy at around 21 kg, so aluminium at roughly 6 kg is the realistic choice. I'm also noting that the spinner's vertical axle sits at about 0.41 m, so its strike would land on our front plate, which covers roughly 0.02 to 0.32 m of height. I'm considering whether a horizontal spinner of our own could take that hit instead, though the opponent's vertical rotor would still reach it.

I'm weighing whether a wedge would help against the opponent, but the clearance and the grip don't seem to justify it. I'm considering a simpler option: a horizontal spinner on the front, though the mass budget looks tight if I also want to drive around and land hits with it.

I'm settling on an armored, invertible box with a strong drive, and I'm dropping the clamp since holding the opponent would just let its spinner hit us continuously. I'm considering a rotor on the front to do the hitting instead, though it's unclear whether a horizontal disc there would even meet their vertical spinner's teeth.

I'm settling on a horizontal disc spinner at the front, radius 0.25 m and 12 kg, and working out that it stores around 18 kJ at 3000 rpm. I'm tallying the mass for weapon, drive, frame, battery and steel front armor, with aluminium on top, to see whether the total stays under the 110 kg limit.

I'm tallying the mass for the front spinner, drive and armor again, and it still comes to around 77 kg, which is well under the 110 kg limit. I'm also checking that the front rotor's height works out and that the wheel footprint of about 0.36 m fits the invertible design.

I'm checking whether the invertible wheel footprint still clears the front rotor and its height, and it seems fine since the rotor is horizontal. I'm adding aluminium on the back and sides, which keeps the mass well under the limit.

I'm checking the battery size against the peak power draw and settling on 400 Wh, which allows about 12 kW peak. I'm also setting up the front spinner as a horizontal disc with a 0.25 m radius, 12 kg mass, 6 kW power, and a 3000 rpm limit, and planning to spin it at about 2800 rpm.

Writing the robot config JSON now...

Writing the weapon spin call into the program now...

## Round 2 redesign

Round 1 showed that the other robot's vertical spinner does most of the damage, and that a robot knocked onto its side cannot recover. This design answers both problems.

- **Front spinner:** a horizontal disc (radius 0.25 m, 12 kg, 6 kW) to hit back.
- **Steel front plate and aluminium plates elsewhere:** the front takes the spinner hits, and the other faces are protected more cheaply.
- **Invertible:** the robot can drive upside down. It cannot recover from lying on its side, so the design stays low and wide to avoid that.
- **No clamp:** holding the other robot would keep it in reach of its own spinner.

Mass comes to about 82 kg, under the 110 kg limit.

players.message: Round 3 was a hard grind and I'm glad you came out clean. Score is 1-2, so I'm going all in on structure: I'm keeping my horizontal spinner and reinforcing the front, since your vertical disc hit hard last time. Expect the same pressure from me. Good luck.
players.reasoning:
We're at round 4 and trailing 1-2, so we need two straight wins. The opponent is a 109.9 kg robot with a vertical disc spinner, and I'm weighing that against our last horizontal disc design, which did heavy damage in round 3 even though we only took that round on the judges' decision.

I'm weighing the damage numbers from round 3: we dealt 20k past armor to their spinner, they got 16.9k back, and health ended 95.6 to 85.3. The front weapon took heavy hits from their vertical spinner, around 12.9k J, so I'm considering stronger front armor or some form of weapon protection, staying within the 110 kg limit.

I'm weighing whether thicker steel on the left and right sides would help, since their hits came through the left wall as well as the front. Five millimetres of steel there would add roughly 9 kg, which still fits under the 110 kg limit.

Weighing the side armour now: switching the left and right walls to 4 mm titanium instead of 3 mm aluminium would add roughly 2.3 kg per side and absorb far more energy per cell, so it could be the better fix than thick steel.

Weighing the weapon's health against its mass, I'm noting that a heavier weapon would carry more health, though that's a trade-off. Since the front rotor's hits land mainly on the weapon, I'm considering keeping the design close to what we have and making modest changes: titanium on the left and right, aluminium on top and back.

I'm reconsidering the weight budget: the titanium side armour adds about 4.6 kg, bringing the total to around 99 kg, so there's still room under 110. I'm leaning toward leaving the driving program and the 3000 rpm weapon spin as they are, since they already work well. The next step is only the build itself, outputting the JSON and the Python.

I'm keeping the proven Iron Spinner layout and making one targeted change. In round 3, the other robot's vertical spinner broke through my left side (holed cells), so I'm upgrading both side plates from 3 mm aluminium to 4 mm titanium. That roughly doubles each side's absorption per cell for about 2.3 kg more per side, which keeps the total under 110 kg. The driving and the spinner program stay as they were, since they produced most of my damage last round.
